items.q: Seebus plc employed an average of 6,000 people in 2023. During the year 960 left and 720 joined. Calculate its labour turnover.
items.why: Labour turnover = number leaving ÷ average number employed × 100 = 960 ÷ 6,000 × 100 = 16%. The number joining is not part of the calculation.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2025 Q02.1

items.q: A business has revenue of £740,000 and receivables of £110,000. What are its receivables days?
items.why: Receivables days = receivables ÷ revenue × 365 = £110,000 ÷ £740,000 × 365 = 54.3, about 54 days.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business budgeted income of £120m and expenditure of £100m. Actual income was 10% below budget and actual expenditure was 5% below budget. What is the profit variance?
items.why: Budgeted profit = £120m – £100m = £20m. Actual income = £108.00m, actual expenditure = £95.00m, so actual profit = £13.00m. Variance = £13.00m – £20m = £7.00m adverse (profit is lower than budgeted).
items.label: New question

items.q: A company achieved a ROCE of 12% with capital employed of £90m. What was its operating profit?
items.why: ROCE = operating profit ÷ capital employed × 100, so operating profit = ROCE × capital employed = 12% × £90m = £10.8m.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has a gross profit margin of 25% on revenue of £70m. What is its cost of sales?
items.why: Gross profit = 25% × £70m = £17.5m. Cost of sales = revenue – gross profit = £70m – £17.5m = £52.5m.
items.label: New question

items.q: Righton plc, 2024 (£m): non-current assets 335; inventories 80; receivables 35; cash 40; payables 70; net current assets 85; non-current liabilities 230; total equity 190. Righton achieved a ROCE of 12% in 2024. Calculate its operating profit.
items.why: Capital employed = total equity + non-current liabilities = £190m + £230m = £420m. Operating profit = 12% × £420m = £50.4m.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2025 Q17

items.q: The network shows the activities in a project (durations in days). What is the length of the critical path?
items.why: Node 2: earliest start = 3. Node 3: the largest of A+B = 11, A+C = 7 and E = 9, so 11. Node 4: 11 + 2 = 13. The critical path is A–B–D, taking 13 days.
items.label: New question

items.q: A firm's CU is 60%. Capacity then increases by 20%. New CU is:
items.why: Let capacity = 100, so output = 60 (60% CU). New capacity = 100 x 1.2 = 120. Output unchanged at 60. New CU = 60/120 x 100 = 50%. Only capacity increased, not output. More capacity with same output = lower utilisation.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: SCF's cash flow forecast: closing balance on 31 October £4.30m. November: total inflows £3.35m, total outflows £3.22m. The forecast assumed customers pay immediately. From 1 November customers get one month's credit and all take it. Calculate the closing balance for November.
items.why: With one month's credit, November's sales are paid for in December, so November's inflows fall to zero. Closing balance = £4.30m + £0 – £3.22m = £1.08m.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2025 Q01.1

items.q: A product sells for £8. Variable cost per unit is £6 and fixed costs are £7,000. What is the break-even output?
items.why: Contribution per unit = price – variable cost = £8 – £6 = £2. Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit = £7,000 ÷ £2 = 3,500 units.
items.label: New question
